definition_of_a_drop: A family is dropped only when the candidate reads it. For a family it does not read, the drop is the candidate itself and the contrast is the nested one: the candidate with the family added, paired against the candidate. Either way a row is 'the model that reads the family against the model that does not', so a positive mean d and a positive skill say the family helps. This is a judgement call put to her as question 1 on the page; the default applies the rule above.

primary.metric: grid CRPS (23 levels) averaged over leads h = 1..5
primary.also_reported: the Brier score of P(spread > +5 bp) and the coverage of the central 90% band, as in #1349's page
primary.splits: pooled, by lead, by regime and by pressure-day type of the target day (the splits of #1349); groups of fewer than 20 days are listed and not tested

scoring.scorer: repo_model.scoring_protocol (#655), the development tier: no verdict, no registration
scoring.test: scoring_protocol.paired_tests, the studentized stationary bootstrap (ruling 1), mean block 10 business days, 10,000 draws, seed 1483, two-sided 90% interval (the lower end is the one-sided 95% bound); the skill interval and the studentized interval on mean d are reported for every tested row; where the studentized bound cannot be computed the unstudentized percentile interval of mean d is given beside it, with no reading taken from it
scoring.reading: a reading is taken from the mean-d bound (her ruling on #1009): the family helps when the lower end of the 90% interval of mean d is above zero, hurts when the upper end is below zero, otherwise undecided

reading_rules: A figure is a check on days that were already seen. Nothing here is a verdict, nothing is registered and no choice is made on it; (s3c-ann-net) stays the candidate until she rules.
A gain or loss is read from the 90% interval of mean d excluding zero; otherwise undecided. A point estimate alone is not read.
A pooled figure is never read without the lead, regime and pressure-day-type splits beside it.
What a drop is for a family the candidate does not read, the satiation row and the tail-spread row are marked questions with numbered options and a default that changes no claim.
